# Synthetic Data Exchange

A FastAPI service for generating synthetic tabular datasets from a real sample —
train a generative model on your data, sample new rows from it, then score how
statistically close the result is and how much it leaks about the original.

Built on [SDV](https://sdv.dev/) (CTGAN, TVAE, Gaussian Copula) with JWT auth,
schema/constraint management, quality evaluation, and CSV/Excel/SQL/PDF export.

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](./LICENSE)
[![Python 3.9+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.9+-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/downloads/)
[![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-0.104+-green.svg)](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/)

**Scope:** this repository is the backend API only. The React UI shown in the
demo video below is not published here — everything else is driven through the
REST API or the interactive docs at `/docs`.

## Demonstration

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/55ca4a0f-b15b-44b2-98ea-ce3c0b156755

## Why it's built this way

Generating synthetic data is a tradeoff between three things that pull against
each other: **fidelity** (does it look like the real data), **utility** (can you
still train a model on it), and **privacy** (can someone recover a real row).
The design reflects that:

- **Four generation modes** instead of one, because the right model depends on
  how much time you'll accept. Gaussian Copula fits in seconds and captures
  correlations but not complex interactions; CTGAN takes minutes and captures
  much more. Rather than pick for the user, the API exposes the whole spectrum.
- **A model cache** keyed by schema fingerprint, so re-generating from a
  previously seen schema skips training entirely — this is what makes repeated
  calls usable interactively.
- **Constraints layered on top of the model**, because a purely statistical fit
  will happily produce a diastolic blood pressure above systolic, or energy
  consumption uncorrelated with tonnage. Business rules are enforced after
  sampling rather than hoped for.
- **Evaluation as a first-class endpoint**, since synthetic data you haven't
  scored is synthetic data you can't defend.

## Generation modes

| Mode | Endpoint | Typical time | Model |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ultra-fast | `POST /generate/ultra-fast` | seconds | Gaussian Copula |
| Fast | `POST /generate/fast` | seconds–tens of seconds | Gaussian Copula |
| Optimized | `POST /generate/optimized` | tens of seconds, near-instant when cached | auto-selected + cache |
| Balanced | `POST /generate/balanced` | tens of seconds | CTGAN, reduced epochs |
| Default | `POST /generate` | minutes | full CTGAN + constraints |

Timings are rough figures measured on an Apple M2 with ~1,000 rows and 7
columns. They vary a lot with row count, column count and cardinality — use
`POST /generate/benchmark` to measure on your own data rather than trusting
these.

## Quality evaluation

`POST /evaluation/evaluate` compares a real and a synthetic file and returns a
graded report:

- **Statistical similarity** — per-column Kolmogorov–Smirnov tests and
  correlation-matrix preservation.
- **Utility** — trains the same model on real and on synthetic data and compares
  performance, which is the metric that actually matters if you're generating
  training data.
- **Privacy** — membership-inference resistance and k-anonymity checks, to catch
  a model that has memorised rather than generalised.

Scores are combined into an A–F grade. Treat the grade as a smoke test, not a
compliance artifact.

## Running it

Requires Python 3.9+.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/david-g-3654/synthetic-data-exchange
cd synthetic-data-exchange

python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate          # Windows: venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt

cp .env.example .env
# Set SECRET_KEY to a random value — the app will refuse to start without one:
python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))"

uvicorn main:app --reload --port 8000
```

Then open http://localhost:8000/docs for the interactive API docs.

With Docker (reads `SECRET_KEY` from your `.env`):

```bash
docker-compose up --build
```

On Apple Silicon, SDV/PyTorch may need `PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK=1` — see
`fix_mps_issue.py`.

## API examples

Register and get a token. Accounts are identified by email; `/register` returns a
token directly, and `/token` is the standard OAuth2 password form — pass the
email in its `username` field.

```bash
curl -X POST localhost:8000/register \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email":"me@example.com","password":"hunter2"}'

TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/token \
  -d "username=me@example.com&password=hunter2" \
  | python -c "import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['access_token'])")
```

Generate from a CSV:

```bash
curl -X POST localhost:8000/generate/fast \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -F "file=@your_data.csv" -F "num_rows=1000"
```

Score the result:

```bash
curl -X POST localhost:8000/evaluation/evaluate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -F "real_data_file=@original.csv" \
  -F "synthetic_data_file=@synthetic.csv"
```

Generate from a built-in industry template, and export as Excel:

```bash
curl localhost:8000/schemas/templates

curl -X POST localhost:8000/advanced-types/timeseries/energy \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -F "num_rows=1000" -F "frequency=H" -F "export_format=xlsx"

curl -X POST localhost:8000/export/data/xlsx \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -F "file=@synthetic_data.csv"
```

Full route list is at `/docs`; `GET /schemas/domains` and
`GET /advanced-types/supported` enumerate what's available.

## Industry templates

Prebuilt schemas with domain constraints attached:

| Domain | Example columns | Constraints enforced |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mining | `mine_id, date, tonnage, energy_used, ore_grade` | energy ≈ 2.5–3.5× tonnage; positive values; chronological dates |
| Healthcare | `patient_id, age, gender, bp_systolic, bp_diastolic` | systolic > diastolic; unique IDs; plausible clinical ranges |
| Energy | `station_id, timestamp, power_output, max_capacity` | output ≤ capacity; efficiency 70–95% |

The healthcare and energy templates exist to *reduce* the amount of real
sensitive data that needs to move around. They are not a compliance
certification — using this for anything regulated is your own due diligence.

## Project structure

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `main.py` | App setup, CORS, router mounting |
| `routers/generate*.py` | The generation modes |
| `routers/auth.py` | Registration, JWT issue/verify |
| `routers/schemas.py` | Schema templates, inference, validation |
| `routers/evaluation.py` | Quality/utility/privacy scoring |
| `routers/exports.py` | CSV, Excel, SQL, PDF export |
| `routers/advanced_types.py` | Time-series, geospatial, healthcare generators |
| `model_manager.py` | Model selection, training, cache |
| `constraints_manager.py` | Business-rule enforcement |
| `evaluation_manager.py` | The metrics behind the grades |
| `security.py` | JWT config, read from the environment |

## Tech stack

FastAPI · SDV (CTGAN / TVAE / Gaussian Copula) · SQLAlchemy + SQLite ·
PyJWT + passlib/bcrypt · pandas · ReportLab (PDF) · OpenPyXL (Excel) · Docker

## Known limitations

- **No test suite.** The largest gap in the project.
- SQLite by default; would need PostgreSQL for concurrent use.
- No rate limiting, and uploads are bounded only by `MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB`.
- Geospatial generation degrades to a warning if GeoPandas isn't installed
  rather than failing clearly.
- The privacy metrics are heuristics. They are useful for catching obvious
  memorisation, not for making a formal differential-privacy guarantee.
- The React frontend is not in this repository.
